gen-dafont-origami-gf-oxygen: Oxygen keeps its curves open and its lowercase tall. Origami hits back with a brush-stroke heading whose stems and curves all share one width, so the two feel like a poured-lead slab sitting beside a plain sans that barely closes a letter.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-parkinsans: Origami looks hand-painted, one brush stroke at a constant width. Its heavy lowercase is best at making a statement, while Parkinsans, a sans-serif with wide-mouthed letters, stays crisp even when shrunk.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-pathway-extreme: A single-stroke brush look, with no calligraphic thinning anywhere, defines Origami. Pathway Extreme sits beneath it with a big x-height and stubby ascenders, and its size can go up a notch if you want the plain sans to hold its own.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-preahvihear: Origami lays down heavy lowercase with stroke ends as wide as the middle, while Preahvihear opens each letter like a pried oyster shell. The result is pure contrast.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-puritan: Origami paints every letter from one width of stroke, dense as poured lead type. Puritan follows with rounded forms that stay open to the side, and giving it a little extra size shows off those generous counters.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-radio-canada-big: Radio Canada Big fills the line with a monoline skeleton and terminals that finish well clear of the stem. Under Origami's brushy heft, paragraphs would move along smoothly.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-ruda: Approachable from the first line, Ruda is a sans-serif with a wire-like monoline skeleton and wide-mouthed rounds. And Origami's brushed, lead-heavy lowercase gives it something solid to lean against.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-saira: Hollow glass-tube lettering, constant thickness throughout. Origami made small would lose that tube-like character, and Saira at large sizes would lose the see-through gap in each s that makes it a crisp sans-serif.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-sofia-sans-semi-co: Origami brings a sign-painter's single-stroke brush look and a lowercase mass like poured lead type. And its weight earns its keep when big and short, with Sofia Sans Semi Condensed nearly matching capital height below.
gen-dafont-origami-gf-stack-sans-headlin: Origami's single-stroke brush look at constant width gives it a hand-painted, lead-heavy presence. Stack Sans Headline, a sans-serif, does the quieter work, with wide gaps that keep tiny sizes crisp and a deep middle band.
